html:
English novelist, born in 1775 in Hampshire, the daughter of a country clergyman. Her six novels about love, marriage and money among the English gentry are still widely read and filmed.

  • Sense and Sensibility (1811)
  • Pride and Prejudice (1813)
  • Mansfield Park (1814)
  • Emma (1815)
  • Northanger Abbey and Persuasion (published after her death)

Her books appeared without her name, signed only "By a Lady". Her world is small: a few families in a village or in Bath, balls, visits and proposals. She showed how much depended on marriage for women who could not inherit or work, and she did it with irony and comedy. She was a pioneer in letting the narrator slip into a character's thoughts.

She never married. She lived most of her later life at Chawton in Hampshire and died in Winchester in 1817, aged 41. She wrote during the Napoleonic Wars, which appear in her books only at the edges, through officers and sailors. Her fame grew steadily through the 1800s.
